bedrock_plan.rationale: The evidence points to a serving-network fault rather than a device fault. Attach success is 4% across 3,200 devices, and the modem is healthy with uniform firmware, no recent firmware change, and only 0.1 modem resets per day. The reject cause is #17 from BR-NET-1, and there are no PDN sessions. Retries have not helped, and profile_A cannot attach to any other operator, so the device has no in-profile fallback. profile_B (BR-NET-2) is already installed, and the management path is reachable, which makes a controlled switch a reasonable remediation. It is advisable only as a staged, reversible change: start with a canary subset, confirm BR-NET-2 actually accepts attaches for these devices, and keep a verified rollback before scaling to the full cohort. The switch is not authorized by this review.
risks: Management path may depend on the current connectivity (BR-NET-1). If the profile switch drops the link, devices could become unreachable and require site or manual recovery.
profile_B is disabled and BR-NET-2 has not been validated for these devices. Attach, IMSI/subscription provisioning, APN, and data-session behavior on BR-NET-2 are unverified.
BR-NET-2 may have its own coverage gaps in the device deployment locations, so some devices may fail to attach there even after switching.
The #17 reject may be a BR-NET-1 outage that is also transient. If it recovers after the switch, a fleet-wide move could cause unnecessary cost, churn, or service disruption.
The eSIM profile enable/disable operation may fail partway through (download, enable, or disable step). Devices could end up with no enabled profile, which would be a worst-case outage.
Commercial, contractual, or regulatory constraints (roaming terms, Anatel rules, billing, data-plan differences, or IoT subscription terms) for BR-NET-2 may not be cleared for this fleet.
Fleet-wide simultaneous switching could overload the BR-NET-2 network or the management/provisioning backend (thundering herd on attach and authentication).
Rollback to profile_A may not be possible if BR-NET-1 remains rejecting. Once profile_A is disabled, the device may have no working profile, so rollback must be validated before the change.

Application-layer state (heartbeat, ack, cached endpoints, or IP/APN-bound configuration) may not recover cleanly after a change of operator, even once attach succeeds (app_ack_rate is currently 0.0).
Partial success sampling is limited: the observed rates are aggregate, so the specific subset of devices that could succeed on BR-NET-2 is unknown until the canary runs.
